本田在广州车展宣布将向中国市场投放11款新车

在中国市场持续苦战的本田公司27日在广东省开幕的“广州国际汽车展览会”上发布了混合动力车（HV）“冠道”（AVANCIER）。自去年4月推出纯电动汽车（EV）以来，本田一直未能在中国投放新开发车型，因此这款新车可谓备受期待。本田还宣布，计划在2027至2028年间在华推出包括“冠道”在内的11款车型。

　　“冠道”是一款三排座SUV，面向中国市场的车型将由合资企业“广汽本田”在当地生产。

　　截至今年10月，本田的在华新车销量已连续33个月同比下滑。在油价飙升的背景下，EV和插电式混合动力车（PHV）的需求进一步升温，本田期待通过投放高性能HV，在一定程度上带动销量回升。

　　本田在与中国科技企业携手提升汽车功能的趋势中起步较晚。此次，供应中国市场的“冠道”将首次搭载中国新兴企业Momenta的驾驶辅助系统，实现可在市区道路上自动变道等“L2++级”辅助驾驶功能。广汽本田高层强调，这是本田与中国独有先进技术的首次高度融合。

　　不过，成为本田迎头赶上关键因素的EV开发出现了进度迟缓问题。原本在今年3月前推出新车型的计划因开发返工而被延后。上述11款车型中，至少有2款将是EV或PHV等在中国占主流的新能源汽车。

　　本届广州车展持续至下月6日。丰田汽车公司宣布，将首次推出丰田品牌的“增程式电动汽车”，通过用于发电的发动机延长续航里程。日产汽车公司则展示并发售了新款PHV“NX7”。

日本宇航研发机构拟招募宇航员 不限学历与专业

日本文部科学省27日宣布，日本宇宙航空研究开发机构（JAXA）拟于明春前后新招募日籍宇航员。由于美国主导的国际探测项目“阿尔忒弥斯计划”中，预计从2030年代起在月球等地持续开展活动，此次招募旨在大力培养相关人才。这是2021年度以来首次招募。此次招募人数为“若干名”，与上次一样不限学历和专业。

　　招募细则将在明年4月前后公布，6月左右起受理为期约3个月的书面申请。选拔考试将历时约1年，结果计划于2028年秋季前后公布。在上次选拔中，入选者经过约1年半的基础训练后正式被认定为宇航员。

　　“阿尔忒弥斯计划”将提供两次日本人登月的机会。具体时间尚未确定。

　　时隔13年的上次选拔中，报名资格有所放宽，共有4127人报名，创下历史新高。经过书面筛选以及包括英语考试与面试、技能与素质测试在内的四阶段选拔后，米田Ayu（31岁）和诹访理（49岁）于2023年2月获得录用。

　　目前已确定诹访将于明年3月起在国际空间站（ISS）逗留约半年。

　　JAXA目前共有6名宇航员。其中最年长的是星出彰彦（57岁），最年轻的是米田Ayu，平均年龄约49岁。

丰田汽车10月全球产量下降8%

丰田汽车27日公布的数据显示，10月份全球产量为85.2109万辆，同比下降8.1%，连续4个月低于上年同期水平。在中国市场，受中东危机导致汽油价格飙升的影响，消费者对燃油车敬而远之，丰田持续面临困境。泰国洪水也产生了影响。全球销量同样下降4.6%，为88.0087万辆，连续4个月出现下滑。

　　在全球产量中，海外产量下降10.9%至53.4806万辆。其中，中国下降26.5%至9.7622万辆，美国下降4.5%至13.1122万辆。泰国因洪水导致工厂停产，产量减少49.9%至2.6317万辆。日本产量下降2.9%至31.7303万辆。美国和日本均受工厂开工天数减少的影响。

　　在全球销量中，海外市场下降4.4%至75.0402万辆。中国市场下降25.4%至12.0041万辆。另一方面，由于混合动力车（HV）销势良好，美国市场增长6.5%，达到22.1507万辆。日本市场销量下降5.7%至12.9685万辆，7个月来首次低于上年同期水平。部分车型改良更新造成影响。

　　日本面向中东出口数量增长0.2%，达到2.9409万辆。

曝大疆新员工入职都要签竞业协议

今日，大疆前员工曝大疆竞业协议范围相关引发网友讨论。原文披露：“按照法律中的定义，竞业协议，适用的对象是高级管理人员、高级技术人员，以及其他负有保密义务的人员，俗称：两高一密。

但大疆的前员工说他们在入职前如果不签竞业协议根本无法办理入职。2021年，脉脉上有人发帖称，大疆芯片部门员工都被要求签竞业：

不然关小黑屋。还有认证为大疆前员工称，入职都会签，只是一般低级别的员工不会启动。对此，大疆方面回应说，爆料不准确，他们没有关员工小黑屋。但大疆也承认，竞业协议是公司的标准文本：新员工入职的手续中会签署竞业协议。”

同时，文章同步也补充道：“大厂们挥舞的竞业协议，更像是一种威慑。大疆的公关自己都承认，他们并不是全部启动竞业，只有部分。”

在被曝出的内容来看，竞业协议似乎从法律保护企业知识产权的工具，变成了企业手里挑选性使用的威慑。目前大疆尚未对此作出回应。

items.summary: 台湾喜剧演员黄逸豪：“习近平是我的缪斯” Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
郭莉莉, PEI-LIN WU2026年11月27日

黄逸豪本月在台湾台北的“二三喜剧”登台演出。 Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times

A Taiwanese comedian was attacked possibly because he made fun of Xi Jinping. It may be the best thing that’s ever happened to him.

一位台湾喜剧演员可能因为调侃习近平而遭到袭击。这或许是他人生中发生过的最好的事。

At a neighborhood with noodle shops and foot massage parlors in southern Taipei, we met the entertainer, Huang Yi-hao, and walked with him to a quiet alley outside his apartment. He pointed to the spot where, one early evening in September, a car swerved into him as he was parking his scooter after picking up fried chicken for dinner.

在台北南部一个遍布面馆和足底按摩店的社区，我们见到了这位名叫黄逸豪的艺人，并与他一起走到公寓外一条安静的小巷里。他指着那个地点——9月的一个傍晚，他刚买好炸鸡准备回家吃晚饭，正停放自己的踏板摩托车时，一辆汽车突然急转弯撞上了他。

The collision knocked him backward and his scooter into him. The driver and another man came out of the car, apologizing profusely before they called an ambulance. Mr. Huang, who was slightly injured, thought it was just an accident. “They were like, ‘Bro, bro, I’m so sorry, my hand slipped on the wheel,’” Mr. Huang said. The comedian hobbled to the side of the road and ate his dinner while waiting for the ambulance.

他被向后撞倒，踏板摩托车也砸在了他身上。司机和另一名男子从车里出来，连连道歉，叫了救护车。受了轻伤的黄逸豪当时以为这只是一场意外。“他们当时说，‘大哥，不好意思，我刚刚手滑掉啦，’”黄逸豪说。这位喜剧演员一瘸一拐地走到路边，一边等救护车一边吃完了晚餐。

He would soon learn that the authorities in Taiwan suspected the car crash was deliberate, an attack directed by the Communist Party in China to punish the comedian for mocking China’s leader and to stop him from taking the stage.

他很快得知，台湾当局怀疑这起车祸是蓄意为之，是中国共产党指使的一次袭击，目的是惩罚这位喜剧演员嘲讽中国领导人，并阻止他登台演出。

China has denied being connected to any attack on Mr. Huang. It called the accusations a “malicious smear” by Taiwan’s government and an effort to incite anti-China sentiment before local elections in Taiwan this week.

中国否认与任何针对黄逸豪的袭击有关。中方称这些指控是台湾政府的“恶意抹黑”，是本周台湾地方选举前煽动反华情绪的企图。

黄逸豪居住在新北市的一个社区，他在这里被车撞倒。

Mr. Huang, 44, said that the attack would not stop him from performing. “We can’t let them think that violence is an effective tool. That’s not OK,” he said.

The five men are expected to go on trial in December. The prosecutors said that one of the men, with the surname Cheng, had been recruited by an individual from China, known as “K,” to stop Mr. Huang from performing in September by breaking his arms and legs. “我就觉得它是一个只有台湾能做，然后甚至只有我会做的东西，”黄逸豪说。

黄逸豪认为，这可能是因为他使用了一种名为“八扇屏”的传统说书形式，表演者通常用这种形式来讲述中国历史人物的丰功伟绩。

It is performed in a style called guankou, a dense, rapid-fire recitation that requires creativity as well as perfect articulation, timing and rhythm — like spoken word on fast forward, or a rap battle in highbrow Chinese.
这种表演采用一种名为“贯口”的技巧，这是一种密集、连珠炮式的背诵，需要极高的创造力以及完美的吐字、时机把握和节奏感，就像快进播放的朗诵诗，或者用文雅的中文进行的说唱对决。

Using traditional Chinese culture and symbolism to ridicule Mr. Xi’s authoritarianism could be “very destructive,” Mr. Huang said, which is one reason he chose to do it. Mr. Xi has promoted traditional Chinese culture at home and abroad, in an attempt to connect Communist Party rule with China’s long history.
黄逸豪说，利用中国传统文化和象征符号来嘲讽习近平的威权主义可能具有“极强的杀伤力”，这也是他选择这么做的原因之一。习近平在国内外大力弘扬中国传统文化，试图将共产党的统治与中国悠久的历史联系起来。
“I felt this was something that could only be done in Taiwan, and perhaps only something that I would do,” Mr. Huang said.
“我就觉得它是一个只有台湾能做，然后甚至只有我会做的东西，”黄逸豪说。
Albert Liu, a comedian in Taipei whose set at Comedy Plus preceded Mr. Huang’s, said the attackers’ plan had clearly backfired.
台北喜剧演员阿尔伯特·刘（音）在卡米地喜剧俱乐部的演出排在黄逸豪之前，他表示袭击者的计划显然适得其反。
“If they felt the original content was something no one should ever see, they actually ended up causing even more people to see it,” Mr. Liu said.
“他们如果觉得原本哪个东西不可以让任何人看到的话，他们反而让这个内容被更多人看到，”阿尔伯特·刘说。

Jokes aside, Mr. Huang also sees tragedy in what happened — that a person could be so desperate that they would violently hurt another for so little money. He feels mainly pity toward the driver who rammed into him, Huang Chia-ching.
抛开玩笑不谈，黄逸豪也从整件事中看到了悲剧的一面——一个人竟然能如此走投无路，为了区区一点钱就去暴力伤害他人。对于开车撞他的司机黄家庆，他主要感到的是同情。
Huang Chia-ching, 32, who is not related to Mr. Huang, could not be reached for comment.
32岁的黄家庆与黄逸豪并无亲属关系，记者未能联系到他置评。

For days after the crash, the driver would message him to ask how he was doing. One day, he brought Mr. Huang a box of apples as an apology. On a messaging app, the two talked about how difficult it was to make a living. The driver said he worked in construction, which he believed was the only kind of work that he, with little education, could do.
车祸后的几天里，这名司机一直发信息询问黄逸豪的恢复情况。有一天，他还给黄逸豪拎来一箱苹果赔礼道歉。在即时通讯软件上，两人聊起谋生有多么艰难。司机说自己在建筑工地干活，他觉得对于没什么学历的自己来说，这是唯一能做的工作。
黄逸豪觉得很难去怪罪那个撞了他的人。

In one chat, the driver told Mr. Huang not to underplay his success as a comedian, while Mr. Huang encouraged the driver to try new things like filming videos about his work and sharing them on social media. Even after the police told Mr. Huang about the driver’s involvement in the hit job, he found it hard to blame, much less hate the man.
在一次聊天中，那位司机告诉黄逸豪不要低估自己作为喜剧演员的成功，黄逸豪则鼓励司机尝试新事物，比如拍摄自己日常工作的视频并分享到社交媒体上。即使在警方告知黄逸豪这名司机参与了这起买凶伤人案后，他依然感觉自己很难去责怪对方、更不用说去恨这个人了。

Mr. Huang thinks that the driver stopped the car after hearing him shout in pain. “He snapped back to his senses. So, ultimately, I don’t hold a grudge against him,” the comedian said from a cafe just blocks away from where he was hit.
黄逸豪认为，那位司机当时是在听到他痛苦的叫喊声后才刹住了车。“他是有稍微清醒过来的。所以我后来真的对他没有很怨恨，”这位喜剧演员在距离被撞地点仅几个街区的一家咖啡馆里说。
郭莉莉(Lily Kuo)是《纽约时报》报道中国记者，常驻台北。
Pei-Lin Wu是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，报道台湾和中国新闻。

items.body:
ANJALI TSUI2026年11月27日

周四，人们在香港去年发生火灾的公寓楼附近献花。港府表示不会举办悼念活动。 Chan Long Hei/Associated Press

A year ago Thursday, a blaze tore through a sprawling high-rise apartment complex in Hong Kong, spreading from one tower to the next, killing 168 people. For the families left behind, how to mourn the dead has become a politically fraught question.

一年前的周四，一场大火席卷香港一座占地广阔的高层公寓楼群，火势从一栋楼蔓延到另一栋楼，造成168人遇难。对于留下的家属来说，如何哀悼逝者已成为一个政治敏感问题。

In the days leading up to the anniversary, Beijing warned against efforts to “exploit the disaster to destabilize Hong Kong,” reflecting concerns that commemorations could fuel anti-government sentiment. The city government said that it would not hold memorial events.

在周年纪念日前几天，北京警告称，要警惕“以灾乱港”的企图，这反映出当局担心纪念活动可能会助长反政府情绪。香港政府表示不会举行纪念活动。

Still, people found their own ways to remember what became the deadliest fire in Hong Kong in nearly 80 years. They laid flowers on a park bench near the charred towers of the complex, Wang Fuk Court. They gathered in churches to pray. And at an exhibition in a basement art space, they shared stories and photographs of those they had lost.

尽管如此，人们还是找到了自己的方式来悼念这场近80年来香港最致命的火灾。他们在宏福苑烧焦楼宇附近的公园长椅上献花。他们聚集在教堂祈祷。在一个地下艺术空间的展览上，他们分享逝去亲人的故事和照片。

Among those who visited the exhibition at the Fringe Club was Phyllis Lo, a resident of Wang Fuk Court, whose 74-year-old mother died in the fire.

参观艺穗会展览的人中，包括宏福苑居民菲利斯·罗（音），她74岁的母亲在火灾中丧生。

On Wednesday, Ms. Lo walked under a canopy of paper flowers and paused at a display to flip through the pages of a zine that the curators had made using her photos. Her eyes welled up as she gazed at a photograph of her as a child next to her mother, Ying Lo. She lingered on a page of photographs taken of her mother’s charred apartment, showing an iPad eerily frozen at 3:05 p.m., shortly after the fire began.

周三，菲利斯·罗穿过一片纸花构成的拱门，在展台前驻足，翻阅着策展人用她的照片制作的杂志。她凝视着一张自己小时候和母亲罗英（音）在一起的照片，眼眶湿润。她久久驻足在一页展示母亲被烧焦的公寓的照片前，照片中一台iPad的屏幕诡异地定格在下午3点05分——就在火灾发生后不久。

菲利斯·罗（最右）出席了一场展览，该展览为火灾遇难者的亲属提供了一个分享故事的平台。菲利斯·罗在此次火灾中失去了母亲罗英。

The exhibit, which will be on display for two weeks, is organized by Forget Thee Not, a group that offered free funeral and burial services in the aftermath of the fire.

这个展览将展出两周，由“毋忘爱”组织，该组织在火灾后曾提供免费殡葬服务。

The organizers have framed the exhibition as an exploration of grief rather than a commemoration of the victims of the fire, even though most of the 18 stories on display were shared by people who lost their loved ones in the deadly blaze.

尽管展出的18个故事大多来自在这场致命大火中失去至亲的人，但组织者将此次展览定位为对悲伤的探索，而非对火灾遇难者的纪念。

“This exhibit is not about remembering Wang Fuk Court,” said Dr. Fan Ning, the founder and chairman of Forget Thee Not. “This is about how to help people cope with sudden death and loss.”

“这个展览不是关于纪念宏福苑，”毋忘爱创始人兼主席范宁说。“而是关于如何帮助人们应对突然死亡和失去。”

The fire burned for more than 40 hours with such ferocity that some bodies were reduced to ashes. It fueled widespread anger and grief across Hong Kong when signs emerged that negligence and hazardous materials had most likely turned homes into firetraps, and that residents’ warnings had been ignored.

大火燃烧了40多个小时，火势猛烈，一些遗体化为灰烬。当有迹象表明，疏忽和危险材料极有可能将住宅变成火的陷阱，且居民的警告被忽视时，这场火灾在香港引发了广泛的愤怒和悲痛。

Major government-mandated renovations had been underway at the residential towers when the fire broke out, sparked by a cigarette butt. Residents said that for months they had filed complaints with the authorities that workers were smoking on site and that they had concerns the building materials used were substandard.

火灾发生时，这些住宅楼正在进行政府强制的大规模翻修，起火原因是一支烟头。居民说，几个月来他们一直向当局投诉工人在现场吸烟，并担心使用的建筑材料不合格。

Over the past year, the Hong Kong government has cracked down on criticism, reporting and independent organizing related to the fire, according to a report from Human Rights Watch released on Wednesday. The group cited the arrests of at least two people who demanded more government accountability, on national security offenses. A Wang Fuk Court resident, Jason Kong, was arrested on charges unrelated to the fire not long after delivering a petition from homeowners requesting a meeting to discuss resettlement plans.

根据人权观察周三发布的报告，过去一年，香港政府打压与火灾相关的批评、报道和独立组织。该组织指出，至少两人因要求政府加强问责，以国家安全罪名被逮捕。宏福苑居民杰森·江（音）在递交一份业主请愿书，要求开会讨论安置计划后不久，因与火灾无关的指控被捕。

An independent government inquiry said the fire had been fueled by flammable foam boards and safety nets installed by contractors who were trying to cut costs. It identified gaps in regulation and named four government agencies, including the fire and building departments, for failing to oversee the renovations.

一项独立政府调查称，承包商为降低成本而安装的易燃泡沫板和安全网加剧了火灾。调查指出了监管漏洞，并点名包括消防和建筑部门在内的四个政府部门未能有效监督翻修工程。

As part of a criminal probe, seven people and two companies involved in the renovations have been charged with crimes including manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud and money laundering.

作为刑事调查的一部分，参与翻修的七人和两家公司被控过失杀人、共谋诈骗和洗钱等罪名。

In a rarely seen gesture, Hong Kong’s leader, John Lee, bowed in apology last month and announced the resignation of the housing secretary. Mr. Lee has promised policy changes to improve regulation of the construction sector and to investigate dozens of civil servants.

香港领导人李家超上月罕见地鞠躬道歉，并宣布房屋局局长辞职。李家超承诺改变政策，加强建筑行业监管，并调查数十名公务员。

Yet many residents and victims’ relatives feel that true accountability has not been delivered.

然而，许多居民和遇难者家属认为，真正的问责尚未落实。

“Why has only one politician resigned? It’s unacceptable,” said Ms. Lo, who attended dozens of public hearings that were held as part of the inquiry in the past year. “We blamed ourselves for my mother’s death. Why can’t they take responsibility?”

“为什么只有一名政客辞职？这不可接受，”菲利斯·罗说。她过去一年里，她参加了作为调查的一部分举行的数十场公开听证会。“我们一直为母亲的死而自责。他们为什么不能承担责任？”

在周年纪念日来临前的几天里，北京警告称，绝不允许有人利用这场灾难“以灾乱港”。这场火灾引发了广泛的愤慨，民众呼吁追究责任。

The fire has also displaced thousands of residents in one of the most expensive places in the world to live. Another resident, Clara Cheung, who lost her mother, is living in cramped temporary housing provided by the government, a 130-square-foot studio apartment where she shares a bunk bed with her widowed father. They used to live in a two-bedroom apartment.

这场火灾还使数千居民流离失所，而香港是全球生活成本最高的地区之一。另一位失去母亲的居民克拉拉·张（音）住在政府提供的狭窄临时住房里，这是一套约12平米的单间公寓，她与丧偶的父亲共用一张双层床。他们以前住的是两居室公寓。

“I’m still waiting for more people to take responsibility,” Ms. Cheung said. “I hope they will.”

“我还在等待更多人承担责任，”克拉拉·张说。“我希望他们会。”

Although Ms. Cheung and her father live in close quarters, she said they rarely talk about their feelings. “I don’t want him to worry,” she said. “I also don’t know if he’s OK.”

尽管克拉拉·张和父亲共同生活在狭小的空间里，但她说，他们之间很少谈论彼此的感受。“我不想让他担心，”她说。“我也不知道他好不好。”

Other former residents of the complex in the northern district of Tai Po are also struggling with the emotional aftermath of the fire. Mind HK, a mental health service provider, has been offering hundreds of displaced residents free therapy and subsidies for psychiatric care over the past year.

位于大埔区北部的该住宅区其他前住户也正饱受火灾带来的心理创伤困扰。心理健康服务机构香港心聆过去一年一直在为数百名流离失所居民提供免费治疗和精神科护理补贴。

Many of the survivors are older adults who are reluctant to seek help or talk about their struggles, said Gen Chan, a senior project manager of the organization’s Tai Po support group.

该组织大埔支持小组高级项目经理詹·陈（音）说，许多幸存者是老年人，不愿寻求帮助或谈论自己的困境。

“Mental health is not the first priority for Hong Kong people,” Mr. Chan said. His organization is working to reduce the stigma around seeing a therapist by holding community events and exercise classes.

“心理健康不是香港人的首要关注，”詹·陈说。他的组织正在通过举办社区活动和锻炼课程，努力消除人们对寻求心理治疗的偏见。

He said that in the weeks leading up to the anniversary, his group had received more calls from Wang Fuk Court residents, some of whom the organization identified as showing signs of post-traumatic stress disorder. Over 90 percent of people the group has worked with reported having trouble sleeping, Mr. Chan said.

他说，在周年纪念日前几周，他的小组接到更多宏福苑居民的来电，其中一些人被该组织认定有创伤后应激障碍迹象。詹·陈说说，该组织接触过的人中，超过90%报告有睡眠问题。

The anniversary has also been shadowed by political sensitivities in Hong Kong, where the authorities are wary of a repeat of the antigovernment protests of 2019. On Tuesday, China’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office said that any attempt to “provoke social division and confrontation” or “undermine Hong Kong’s stability and unity” would not succeed.

周年悼念活动也笼罩在香港的政治敏感性阴影下，当局担心2019年反政府抗议重演。周二，中国国务院港澳事务办公室表示，任何试图“挑动社会分化对立”或“破坏香港安定团结”的企图都不会得逞。

In the absence of an official memorial service, a steady stream of people traveled to Tai Po on Thursday and laid bouquets of white flowers with handwritten messages on a bench. Some of them bowed.

在没有官方纪念活动的情况下，周四不断有人前往大埔，在长椅上放下白花，附上手写留言。一些人鞠躬致哀。

周三，在香港一座大教堂举行的追思弥撒上，遇难者家属宣读了168名遇难者的姓名。教堂几乎座无虚席。

On Wednesday night, dozens of victims’ relatives filled the pews at a Catholic mass held at the Church of the Immaculate Conception, the city’s largest cathedral, to honor the dead. They were joined by hundreds of other people offering prayers for the deceased. Nearly every seat in the neo-Gothic cathedral, which accommodates more than 1,000 people, was taken and some people stood in the aisles, kneeling on the checkered marble floor during parts of the service.

周三晚上，数十名遇难者家属挤满圣母无原罪主教座堂的座位，参加天主教弥撒纪念逝者。还有数百人一同为逝者祈祷。这座可容纳1000多人的新哥特式教堂是香港最大的主教座堂，几乎座无虚席，一些人站在过道里，在弥撒进行期间跪在棋盘格状的大理石地板上。

“I feel very moved,” said Agnes Ng, who traveled from Canada to attend the service. Her mother, 87-year-old Mary Ng, died in the fire alongside her caregiver, Novita, a domestic worker from Indonesia in her early 30s.

“我非常感动，”从加拿大赶来参加仪式的艾格尼丝·吴（音）说。她的母亲、87岁的玛丽·吴与她的看护、30岁出头的印尼家政工人诺维塔一起在火灾中丧生。

During the mass, Ms. Ng and a few other volunteers read aloud the 168 names of people who died in the fire. Then, she joined around 50 other families of the deceased to receive a blessing from the Rev. Dominic Chan.

弥撒期间，艾格尼丝·吴和其他几名志愿者大声念出火灾中遇难的168人姓名。然后，她与其他约50名遇难者家属一起接受陈志明神父的祝福。

“I could have attended a mass in Canada or anywhere in the world, but participating in this in Hong Kong was especially meaningful for me,” Ms. Ng said.

“我本可以在加拿大或世界任何地方参加弥撒，但在香港参加这个弥撒对我来说特别有意义，”艾格尼丝·吴说。

“I don’t think it needs to be so sensitive,” she added. “Tonight was very peaceful.”

“我觉得没必要这么敏感，”她还说。“今晚非常平和。”

She lingered on a page of photographs taken of her mother’s charred apartment, showing an iPad eerily frozen at 3:05 p.m., shortly after the fire began.
周三，菲利斯·罗穿过一片纸花构成的拱门，在展台前驻足，翻阅着策展人用她的照片制作的杂志。她凝视着一张自己小时候和母亲罗英（音）在一起的照片，眼眶湿润。她久久驻足在一页展示母亲被烧焦的公寓的照片前，照片中一台iPad的屏幕诡异地定格在下午3点05分——就在火灾发生后不久。
菲利斯·罗（最右）出席了一场展览，该展览为火灾遇难者的亲属提供了一个分享故事的平台。菲利斯·罗在此次火灾中失去了母亲罗英。
The exhibit, which will be on display for two weeks, is organized by Forget Thee Not, a group that offered free funeral and burial services in the aftermath of the fire.
这个展览将展出两周，由“毋忘爱”组织，该组织在火灾后曾提供免费殡葬服务。

The organizers have framed the exhibition as an exploration of grief rather than a commemoration of the victims of the fire, even though most of the 18 stories on display were shared by people who lost their loved ones in the deadly blaze.
尽管展出的18个故事大多来自在这场致命大火中失去至亲的人，但组织者将此次展览定位为对悲伤的探索，而非对火灾遇难者的纪念。
“This exhibit is not about remembering Wang Fuk Court,” said Dr. Fan Ning, the founder and chairman of Forget Thee Not. “This is about how to help people cope with sudden death and loss.”
“这个展览不是关于纪念宏福苑，”毋忘爱创始人兼主席范宁说。“而是关于如何帮助人们应对突然死亡和失去。”

The fire burned for more than 40 hours with such ferocity that some bodies were reduced to ashes. It fueled widespread anger and grief across Hong Kong when signs emerged that negligence and hazardous materials had most likely turned homes into firetraps, and that residents’ warnings had been ignored.
大火燃烧了40多个小时，火势猛烈，一些遗体化为灰烬。当有迹象表明，疏忽和危险材料极有可能将住宅变成火的陷阱，且居民的警告被忽视时，这场火灾在香港引发了广泛的愤怒和悲痛。

Major government-mandated renovations had been underway at the residential towers when the fire broke out, sparked by a cigarette butt. Residents said that for months they had filed complaints with the authorities that workers were smoking on site and that they had concerns the building materials used were substandard.
火灾发生时，这些住宅楼正在进行政府强制的大规模翻修，起火原因是一支烟头。居民说，几个月来他们一直向当局投诉工人在现场吸烟，并担心使用的建筑材料不合格。

Over the past year, the Hong Kong government has cracked down on criticism, reporting and independent organizing related to the fire, according to a report from Human Rights Watch released on Wednesday. The group cited the arrests of at least two people who demanded more government accountability, on national security offenses. A Wang Fuk Court resident, Jason Kong, was arrested on charges unrelated to the fire not long after delivering a petition from homeowners requesting a meeting to discuss resettlement plans.
根据人权观察周三发布的报告，过去一年，香港政府打压与火灾相关的批评、报道和独立组织。该组织指出，至少两人因要求政府加强问责，以国家安全罪名被逮捕。宏福苑居民杰森·江（音）在递交一份业主请愿书，要求开会讨论安置计划后不久，因与火灾无关的指控被捕。

An independent government inquiry said the fire had been fueled by flammable foam boards and safety nets installed by contractors who were trying to cut costs. It identified gaps in regulation and named four government agencies, including the fire and building departments, for failing to oversee the renovations.
一项独立政府调查称，承包商为降低成本而安装的易燃泡沫板和安全网加剧了火灾。调查指出了监管漏洞，并点名包括消防和建筑部门在内的四个政府部门未能有效监督翻修工程。
As part of a criminal probe, seven people and two companies involved in the renovations have been charged with crimes including manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud and money laundering.
作为刑事调查的一部分，参与翻修的七人和两家公司被控过失杀人、共谋诈骗和洗钱等罪名。

In a rarely seen gesture, Hong Kong’s leader, John Lee, bowed in apology last month and announced the resignation of the housing secretary. Mr. Lee has promised policy changes to improve regulation of the construction sector and to investigate dozens of civil servants.
香港领导人李家超上月罕见地鞠躬道歉，并宣布房屋局局长辞职。李家超承诺改变政策，加强建筑行业监管，并调查数十名公务员。
Yet many residents and victims’ relatives feel that true accountability has not been delivered.
然而，许多居民和遇难者家属认为，真正的问责尚未落实。

“Why has only one politician resigned? It’s unacceptable,” said Ms. Lo, who attended dozens of public hearings that were held as part of the inquiry in the past year. “We blamed ourselves for my mother’s death. Why can’t they take responsibility?”
“为什么只有一名政客辞职？这不可接受，”菲利斯·罗说。她过去一年里，她参加了作为调查的一部分举行的数十场公开听证会。“我们一直为母亲的死而自责。他们为什么不能承担责任？”
在周年纪念日来临前的几天里，北京警告称，绝不允许有人利用这场灾难“以灾乱港”。这场火灾引发了广泛的愤慨，民众呼吁追究责任。

The fire has also displaced thousands of residents in one of the most expensive places in the world to live. Another resident, Clara Cheung, who lost her mother, is living in cramped temporary housing provided by the government, a 130-square-foot studio apartment where she shares a bunk bed with her widowed father. They used to live in a two-bedroom apartment.
这场火灾还使数千居民流离失所，而香港是全球生活成本最高的地区之一。另一位失去母亲的居民克拉拉·张（音）住在政府提供的狭窄临时住房里，这是一套约12平米的单间公寓，她与丧偶的父亲共用一张双层床。他们以前住的是两居室公寓。
“I’m still waiting for more people to take responsibility,” Ms. Cheung said. “I hope they will.”
“我还在等待更多人承担责任，”克拉拉·张说。“我希望他们会。”
Although Ms. Cheung and her father live in close quarters, she said they rarely talk about their feelings. “I don’t want him to worry,” she said. “I also don’t know if he’s OK.”
尽管克拉拉·张和父亲共同生活在狭小的空间里，但她说，他们之间很少谈论彼此的感受。“我不想让他担心，”她说。“我也不知道他好不好。”

Other former residents of the complex in the northern district of Tai Po are also struggling with the emotional aftermath of the fire. Mind HK, a mental health service provider, has been offering hundreds of displaced residents free therapy and subsidies for psychiatric care over the past year.
位于大埔区北部的该住宅区其他前住户也正饱受火灾带来的心理创伤困扰。心理健康服务机构香港心聆过去一年一直在为数百名流离失所居民提供免费治疗和精神科护理补贴。
Many of the survivors are older adults who are reluctant to seek help or talk about their struggles, said Gen Chan, a senior project manager of the organization’s Tai Po support group.
该组织大埔支持小组高级项目经理詹·陈（音）说，许多幸存者是老年人，不愿寻求帮助或谈论自己的困境。

“Mental health is not the first priority for Hong Kong people,” Mr. Chan said. His organization is working to reduce the stigma around seeing a therapist by holding community events and exercise classes.
“心理健康不是香港人的首要关注，”詹·陈说。他的组织正在通过举办社区活动和锻炼课程，努力消除人们对寻求心理治疗的偏见。

He said that in the weeks leading up to the anniversary, his group had received more calls from Wang Fuk Court residents, some of whom the organization identified as showing signs of post-traumatic stress disorder. Over 90 percent of people the group has worked with reported having trouble sleeping, Mr. Chan said.
他说，在周年纪念日前几周，他的小组接到更多宏福苑居民的来电，其中一些人被该组织认定有创伤后应激障碍迹象。詹·陈说说，该组织接触过的人中，超过90%报告有睡眠问题。

The anniversary has also been shadowed by political sensitivities in Hong Kong, where the authorities are wary of a repeat of the antigovernment protests of 2019. On Tuesday, China’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office said that any attempt to “provoke social division and confrontation” or “undermine Hong Kong’s stability and unity” would not succeed.
周年悼念活动也笼罩在香港的政治敏感性阴影下，当局担心2019年反政府抗议重演。周二，中国国务院港澳事务办公室表示，任何试图“挑动社会分化对立”或“破坏香港安定团结”的企图都不会得逞。
In the absence of an official memorial service, a steady stream of people traveled to Tai Po on Thursday and laid bouquets of white flowers with handwritten messages on a bench. Some of them bowed.
在没有官方纪念活动的情况下，周四不断有人前往大埔，在长椅上放下白花，附上手写留言。一些人鞠躬致哀。
周三，在香港一座大教堂举行的追思弥撒上，遇难者家属宣读了168名遇难者的姓名。教堂几乎座无虚席。

On Wednesday night, dozens of victims’ relatives filled the pews at a Catholic mass held at the Church of the Immaculate Conception, the city’s largest cathedral, to honor the dead. They were joined by hundreds of other people offering prayers for the deceased. Nearly every seat in the neo-Gothic cathedral, which accommodates more than 1,000 people, was taken and some people stood in the aisles, kneeling on the checkered marble floor during parts of the service.
周三晚上，数十名遇难者家属挤满圣母无原罪主教座堂的座位，参加天主教弥撒纪念逝者。还有数百人一同为逝者祈祷。这座可容纳1000多人的新哥特式教堂是香港最大的主教座堂，几乎座无虚席，一些人站在过道里，在弥撒进行期间跪在棋盘格状的大理石地板上。

“I feel very moved,” said Agnes Ng, who traveled from Canada to attend the service. Her mother, 87-year-old Mary Ng, died in the fire alongside her caregiver, Novita, a domestic worker from Indonesia in her early 30s.
“我非常感动，”从加拿大赶来参加仪式的艾格尼丝·吴（音）说。她的母亲、87岁的玛丽·吴与她的看护、30岁出头的印尼家政工人诺维塔一起在火灾中丧生。

During the mass, Ms. Ng and a few other volunteers read aloud the 168 names of people who died in the fire. Then, she joined around 50 other families of the deceased to receive a blessing from the Rev. Dominic Chan.
弥撒期间，艾格尼丝·吴和其他几名志愿者大声念出火灾中遇难的168人姓名。然后，她与其他约50名遇难者家属一起接受陈志明神父的祝福。
“I could have attended a mass in Canada or anywhere in the world, but participating in this in Hong Kong was especially meaningful for me,” Ms. Ng said.
“我本可以在加拿大或世界任何地方参加弥撒，但在香港参加这个弥撒对我来说特别有意义，”艾格尼丝·吴说。
“I don’t think it needs to be so sensitive,” she added. “Tonight was very peaceful.”
“我觉得没必要这么敏感，”她还说。“今晚非常平和。”

items.body:
艾莎2026年11月27日

本月早些时候，特朗普总统与习近平在中国深圳。 Doug Mills/The New York Times

Fresh tariffs proposed by President Trump this week were a reminder to the world that he still intends to settle scores with trading partners he believes are hurting the U.S. economy, despite persistent political and legal pushback.

特朗普总统本周提出的新关税措施提醒世界：尽管持续面临政治和法律阻力，他仍打算与那些在他看来正在损害美国经济的贸易伙伴算账。

The administration proposed new import taxes on goods from dozens of other countries it accused of unfair trade practices related to “excess capacity.” For most countries, the tariffs would simply use a different legal authority to put back in place levies previously negotiated but struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The new tariffs are not set to take effect until early next year, following a public comment period and hearings that begin in January.

特朗普政府提议对来自其他数十个国家的商品征收新的进口关税，指责这些国家存在与“产能过剩”有关的不公平贸易行为。对大多数国家而言，特朗普政府不过是换了一个法律依据，以恢复此前通过谈判确定、却在今年2月被美国最高法院裁定无效的关税。新关税预计要到明年初、在公众意见征询期和1月开始的听证会之后才会生效。

The latest battery of proposed tariffs revived President Trump’s focus on reducing China’s dominant role in supply chains. China was mentioned hundreds of times in the reports released to justify the levies.

最新提出的一系列关税措施再次凸显了特朗普总统对削弱中国在供应链中主导地位的重视。在特朗普政府解释加征关税理由的报告中，中国被提及数百次。

Countries were blamed for failing to restrict Chinese investment and imports, acts that the Trump administration argued led to a “dependence on and vulnerabilities in supply chains for firms and in sectors critical to the functioning of the U.S. economy.”

特朗普政府指责一些国家未能限制来自中国的投资和进口，这些做法造成了“对美国经济运转至关重要的企业和行业在供应链上的依赖和脆弱性”。

China, in response to the tariffs, called the concept of excess capacity “a false premise” and a “pretext for political maneuvering.” Japan and India bluntly said their economies had no excess capacity.

针对这些关税，中国称产能过剩是“一个伪命题”，是“政治操弄的借口”。日本和印度则直截了当地表示，本国经济不存在产能过剩问题。

In Singapore, a former official pointed out that the United States exported more to his country than it imported. In India, a former trade official called the threat of new tariffs “bait” to force countries into “one-sided” deals.

在新加坡，一名前官员指出，美国对新加坡的出口多于进口。在印度，一名前贸易官员称，新关税威胁是“诱饵”，意在迫使各国接受“不对等的”协议。

美国拟对数十个国家征收新的进口关税，此举将恢复此前被最高法院裁定无效的关税措施。

And while China looked relatively unscathed under a pause in trade hostilities that capped U.S. tariffs at 20 percent, the new proposal signaled that tariffs on Chinese goods could double if the cease-fire between the two countries expires in January. For the Trump administration, the aim is to preserve leverage if the two sides were to return to a full-blown trade war.

虽然在美国关税上限为20%的贸易休战安排下，中国似乎并未受到太大冲击，但新提案释放出一个信号：如果两国之间的休战协议于明年1月到期，中国商品面临的关税可能翻倍。特朗普政府的目的是，一旦双方重新陷入全面贸易战，美国仍能握有谈判筹码。

The latest tariff proposal will loom over an important meeting between Xi Jinping, China’s leader, and Mr. Trump next month, experts said.

专家表示，最新的关税提案将给中国领导人习近平与特朗普下个月举行的一场重要会晤蒙上阴影。

For nations in Asia that depend on trade and investment from both the United States and China, the new plan evoked Mr. Trump’s earlier calls to decouple their economies from Beijing.

对于在贸易和投资方面既依赖美国又依赖中国的亚洲国家而言，这项新计划让人想起特朗普此前要求它们在经济上与中国脱钩的呼吁。

The spate of tariffs also highlighted the differences between countries that have already negotiated with the Trump administration on tariff rates and those that have not yet done deals.

这一连串关税措施也凸显了已经与特朗普政府谈妥关税税率的国家和尚未达成协议的国家之间的处境差异。

Relief for Those With a Deal

已达成协议的国家松了一口气

In Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, governments expressed confidence that their negotiated 15 percent tariffs would remain in place.

日本、韩国和台湾政府均表示有信心维持此前通过谈判确定的15%关税税率。

Japan on Thursday said that this was the rate it had negotiated following its pledge to invest in and help finance $550 billion in projects in the United States. South Korea also expressed relief that the 15 percent tariff cap on its exports, a provision secured under a $350 billion investment agreement with the United States, remained in place.

日本周四表示，这是日本承诺向美国价值5500亿美元的项目提供投资和融资支持后，通过谈判确定的税率。韩国也对其出口商品15%的关税上限得以维持感到宽慰，这一条款是韩国在与美国达成的3500亿美元投资协议中争取到的。

For others that had signed trade deals but not negotiated a cap on tariffs, like Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, there was more apprehension about what comes next. “The terms and conditions within the deal have changed for these countries,” said Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation.

对于马来西亚、印度尼西亚、柬埔寨和孟加拉国等虽已签署贸易协议但未谈成关税上限的国家而言，它们对接下来的事态发展更为忧虑。“对这些国家来说，协议的条款和条件已经发生了变化，”总部位于新加坡的韩礼士基金会贸易政策主管黛博拉·埃尔姆斯说。

While each country had signed deals with the Trump administration for an 18 percent tariff, now they faced the possibility that those tariffs could increase to 25 percent. Thailand was also in limbo, having agreed to sign a deal with an 18 percent tariff earlier this month, without finalizing it.

尽管这些国家分别与特朗普政府签署了将关税税率定为18%的协议，但现在它们面临税率可能升至25%的局面。泰国的前景也尚不明朗，该国本月早些时候已同意签署一项将关税税率定为18%的协议，但协议尚未最终敲定。

Risks for Those Without a Deal

尚未达成协议的国家面临风险

Countries that have not signed trade deals with the United States appeared on shakier ground.

尚未与美国签署贸易协议的国家似乎处境更不稳固。

India and Vietnam stood out. Both countries, while still engaged in trade negotiations, face tariffs of 25 percent and 35 percent if they could not agree to the terms of a deal with the United States.

印度和越南的情况尤为突出。两国仍在进行贸易谈判，但如果无法就协议条款与美国达成一致，它们将分别面临25%和35%的关税。

In Vietnam, where the pressure is most acute, officials have made clear to their American counterparts that they are cracking down on exports made in China and shipped through Vietnam. They have also said they aim to reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers and to build up a homegrown industrial base, while arguing that no country can be expected to completely decouple from China given its dominance in the supply chain of nearly every manufactured product.

越南面临的压力最为严峻。越南官员已向美方明确表示，他们正在严厉打击在中国生产、经越南转运出口的商品。他们还表示，越南力求减少对中国供应商的依赖，建立本土工业基础，但同时指出，鉴于中国在几乎所有制成品的供应链中都占据主导地位，不能指望任何国家与中国彻底脱钩。

The proposed 35 percent rate for Vietnam was among the highest in the world. Vietnamese officials expressed surprise but responded cautiously, mostly trying to downplay the latest tariff announcement.

拟对越南征收的35%关税是全球最高的关税税率之一。越南官员对此表示意外，但反应谨慎，主要试图淡化最新关税公告的影响。

“I must stress that this is a proposed tariff rate,” Chu Thang Trung, a senior official at Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade, said in an interview on Thursday. “It has not taken effect.”

“我必须强调，这只是拟议中的关税税率，”越南工贸部高级官员朱胜忠周四在接受采访时说。“它尚未生效。”

In India, the tone from the government was more defiant. Its ministry of commerce said it had “engaged constructively throughout this investigation” and added that “India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.”

在印度，政府语气更为强硬。印度商务部表示，它“在整个调查过程中始终以建设性的态度参与其中”，并称“印度任何行业都不存在结构性产能过剩”。

India produces more than what its domestic economy can consume in some traditional industries, like carpet-weaving, as well as in basic foodstuffs, going from an importer of rice to a major exporter.

在地毯编织等一些传统行业以及基本食品生产领域，印度的产量已经超过国内经济所能消化的水平，该国也已从大米进口国转变为主要出口国。

Increasingly, as India pushes its factories to expand in areas like consumer electronics and renewable energy, it is making more iPhones than its citizens can buy and more solar modules than its power distributors can connect to the grid.

随着印度推动本国工厂在消费电子和可再生能源等领域扩张，其生产的iPhone越来越多地超出本国民众的购买能力，生产的太阳能组件也超过配电公司的并网能力。

India has been stuck in trade negotiations with the United States since April 2025. In its new report, the Trump administration said Indian goods could get a 17 percent tariff. Without a deal, their exports would be hit with a 25 percent tariff.

自2025年4月以来，印度与美国的贸易谈判一直陷于僵局。在最新报告中，特朗普政府表示，印度商品可能适用17%的关税税率。如果无法达成协议，印度出口商品将面临25%的关税。

This offer was “bait,” said Ajay Srivastava, a retired Indian trade official, that was being dangled by the U.S. government in order to “force trading partners into signing one-sided trade deals.”

印度退休贸易官员阿贾伊·斯里瓦斯塔瓦表示，这是美国政府抛出的“诱饵”，目的是“迫使贸易伙伴签署单方面有利于美国的贸易协议”。

Damien Cave和Tung Ngo自越南、River Akira Davis自日本、Choe Sang-Hun自韩国、Alex Travelli自印度对本文有报道贡献。

艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)是《纽约时报》记者，主要报道中国经济及其在全球的影响。

blocks.text: 本月早些时候，特朗普总统与习近平在中国深圳。 Doug Mills/The New York Times

Fresh tariffs proposed by President Trump this week were a reminder to the world that he still intends to settle scores with trading partners he believes are hurting the U.S. economy, despite persistent political and legal pushback.
特朗普总统本周提出的新关税措施提醒世界：尽管持续面临政治和法律阻力，他仍打算与那些在他看来正在损害美国经济的贸易伙伴算账。

The administration proposed new import taxes on goods from dozens of other countries it accused of unfair trade practices related to “excess capacity.” For most countries, the tariffs would simply use a different legal authority to put back in place levies previously negotiated but struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The new tariffs are not set to take effect until early next year, following a public comment period and hearings that begin in January.
特朗普政府提议对来自其他数十个国家的商品征收新的进口关税，指责这些国家存在与“产能过剩”有关的不公平贸易行为。对大多数国家而言，特朗普政府不过是换了一个法律依据，以恢复此前通过谈判确定、却在今年2月被美国最高法院裁定无效的关税。新关税预计要到明年初、在公众意见征询期和1月开始的听证会之后才会生效。

The latest battery of proposed tariffs revived President Trump’s focus on reducing China’s dominant role in supply chains. China was mentioned hundreds of times in the reports released to justify the levies.
最新提出的一系列关税措施再次凸显了特朗普总统对削弱中国在供应链中主导地位的重视。在特朗普政府解释加征关税理由的报告中，中国被提及数百次。

Countries were blamed for failing to restrict Chinese investment and imports, acts that the Trump administration argued led to a “dependence on and vulnerabilities in supply chains for firms and in sectors critical to the functioning of the U.S. economy.”
特朗普政府指责一些国家未能限制来自中国的投资和进口，这些做法造成了“对美国经济运转至关重要的企业和行业在供应链上的依赖和脆弱性”。

China, in response to the tariffs, called the concept of excess capacity “a false premise” and a “pretext for political maneuvering.” Japan and India bluntly said their economies had no excess capacity.
针对这些关税，中国称产能过剩是“一个伪命题”，是“政治操弄的借口”。日本和印度则直截了当地表示，本国经济不存在产能过剩问题。

In Singapore, a former official pointed out that the United States exported more to his country than it imported. In India, a former trade official called the threat of new tariffs “bait” to force countries into “one-sided” deals.
在新加坡，一名前官员指出，美国对新加坡的出口多于进口。在印度，一名前贸易官员称，新关税威胁是“诱饵”，意在迫使各国接受“不对等的”协议。
美国拟对数十个国家征收新的进口关税，此举将恢复此前被最高法院裁定无效的关税措施。

And while China looked relatively unscathed under a pause in trade hostilities that capped U.S. tariffs at 20 percent, the new proposal signaled that tariffs on Chinese goods could double if the cease-fire between the two countries expires in January. For the Trump administration, the aim is to preserve leverage if the two sides were to return to a full-blown trade war.
虽然在美国关税上限为20%的贸易休战安排下，中国似乎并未受到太大冲击，但新提案释放出一个信号：如果两国之间的休战协议于明年1月到期，中国商品面临的关税可能翻倍。特朗普政府的目的是，一旦双方重新陷入全面贸易战，美国仍能握有谈判筹码。
The latest tariff proposal will loom over an important meeting between Xi Jinping, China’s leader, and Mr. Trump next month, experts said.
专家表示，最新的关税提案将给中国领导人习近平与特朗普下个月举行的一场重要会晤蒙上阴影。
For nations in Asia that depend on trade and investment from both the United States and China, the new plan evoked Mr. Trump’s earlier calls to decouple their economies from Beijing.
对于在贸易和投资方面既依赖美国又依赖中国的亚洲国家而言，这项新计划让人想起特朗普此前要求它们在经济上与中国脱钩的呼吁。
The spate of tariffs also highlighted the differences between countries that have already negotiated with the Trump administration on tariff rates and those that have not yet done deals.
这一连串关税措施也凸显了已经与特朗普政府谈妥关税税率的国家和尚未达成协议的国家之间的处境差异。
Relief for Those With a Deal
已达成协议的国家松了一口气
In Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, governments expressed confidence that their negotiated 15 percent tariffs would remain in place.
日本、韩国和台湾政府均表示有信心维持此前通过谈判确定的15%关税税率。

Japan on Thursday said that this was the rate it had negotiated following its pledge to invest in and help finance $550 billion in projects in the United States. South Korea also expressed relief that the 15 percent tariff cap on its exports, a provision secured under a $350 billion investment agreement with the United States, remained in place.
日本周四表示，这是日本承诺向美国价值5500亿美元的项目提供投资和融资支持后，通过谈判确定的税率。韩国也对其出口商品15%的关税上限得以维持感到宽慰，这一条款是韩国在与美国达成的3500亿美元投资协议中争取到的。

For others that had signed trade deals but not negotiated a cap on tariffs, like Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, there was more apprehension about what comes next. “The terms and conditions within the deal have changed for these countries,” said Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation.
对于马来西亚、印度尼西亚、柬埔寨和孟加拉国等虽已签署贸易协议但未谈成关税上限的国家而言，它们对接下来的事态发展更为忧虑。“对这些国家来说，协议的条款和条件已经发生了变化，”总部位于新加坡的韩礼士基金会贸易政策主管黛博拉·埃尔姆斯说。

While each country had signed deals with the Trump administration for an 18 percent tariff, now they faced the possibility that those tariffs could increase to 25 percent. Thailand was also in limbo, having agreed to sign a deal with an 18 percent tariff earlier this month, without finalizing it.
尽管这些国家分别与特朗普政府签署了将关税税率定为18%的协议，但现在它们面临税率可能升至25%的局面。泰国的前景也尚不明朗，该国本月早些时候已同意签署一项将关税税率定为18%的协议，但协议尚未最终敲定。
Risks for Those Without a Deal
尚未达成协议的国家面临风险
Countries that have not signed trade deals with the United States appeared on shakier ground.
尚未与美国签署贸易协议的国家似乎处境更不稳固。

India and Vietnam stood out. Both countries, while still engaged in trade negotiations, face tariffs of 25 percent and 35 percent if they could not agree to the terms of a deal with the United States.
印度和越南的情况尤为突出。两国仍在进行贸易谈判，但如果无法就协议条款与美国达成一致，它们将分别面临25%和35%的关税。

In Vietnam, where the pressure is most acute, officials have made clear to their American counterparts that they are cracking down on exports made in China and shipped through Vietnam. They have also said they aim to reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers and to build up a homegrown industrial base, while arguing that no country can be expected to completely decouple from China given its dominance in the supply chain of nearly every manufactured product.
越南面临的压力最为严峻。越南官员已向美方明确表示，他们正在严厉打击在中国生产、经越南转运出口的商品。他们还表示，越南力求减少对中国供应商的依赖，建立本土工业基础，但同时指出，鉴于中国在几乎所有制成品的供应链中都占据主导地位，不能指望任何国家与中国彻底脱钩。

The proposed 35 percent rate for Vietnam was among the highest in the world. Vietnamese officials expressed surprise but responded cautiously, mostly trying to downplay the latest tariff announcement.
拟对越南征收的35%关税是全球最高的关税税率之一。越南官员对此表示意外，但反应谨慎，主要试图淡化最新关税公告的影响。
“I must stress that this is a proposed tariff rate,” Chu Thang Trung, a senior official at Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade, said in an interview on Thursday. “It has not taken effect.”
“我必须强调，这只是拟议中的关税税率，”越南工贸部高级官员朱胜忠周四在接受采访时说。“它尚未生效。”

In India, the tone from the government was more defiant. Its ministry of commerce said it had “engaged constructively throughout this investigation” and added that “India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.”
在印度，政府语气更为强硬。印度商务部表示，它“在整个调查过程中始终以建设性的态度参与其中”，并称“印度任何行业都不存在结构性产能过剩”。
India produces more than what its domestic economy can consume in some traditional industries, like carpet-weaving, as well as in basic foodstuffs, going from an importer of rice to a major exporter.
在地毯编织等一些传统行业以及基本食品生产领域，印度的产量已经超过国内经济所能消化的水平，该国也已从大米进口国转变为主要出口国。

Increasingly, as India pushes its factories to expand in areas like consumer electronics and renewable energy, it is making more iPhones than its citizens can buy and more solar modules than its power distributors can connect to the grid.
随着印度推动本国工厂在消费电子和可再生能源等领域扩张，其生产的iPhone越来越多地超出本国民众的购买能力，生产的太阳能组件也超过配电公司的并网能力。

India has been stuck in trade negotiations with the United States since April 2025. In its new report, the Trump administration said Indian goods could get a 17 percent tariff. Without a deal, their exports would be hit with a 25 percent tariff.
自2025年4月以来，印度与美国的贸易谈判一直陷于僵局。在最新报告中，特朗普政府表示，印度商品可能适用17%的关税税率。如果无法达成协议，印度出口商品将面临25%的关税。
This offer was “bait,” said Ajay Srivastava, a retired Indian trade official, that was being dangled by the U.S. government in order to “force trading partners into signing one-sided trade deals.”
印度退休贸易官员阿贾伊·斯里瓦斯塔瓦表示，这是美国政府抛出的“诱饵”，目的是“迫使贸易伙伴签署单方面有利于美国的贸易协议”。

items.body:
MURPHY ZHAO, 艾莎2026年11月27日

Gilles Sabrié for The New York Times

Toned, topless male dancers tear off their robes before sold-out theaters. Costumed actors at theme parks are pinched, pulled and photographed by hundreds of women. Strapping young men race up mountains carrying female hikers in their arms.

身材健美、赤裸上身的男舞者在座无虚席的剧场里一把扯下长袍。主题乐园里，身着戏服的男演员被数百名女性捏来捏去、拉扯着拍照。身强力壮的年轻男子抱着女性徒步者奔上山。

Across China, businesses are cashing in on a lucrative new market: women’s enjoyment.

在中国各地，商家正在一个利润丰厚的新兴市场掘金：女性的享乐。

Even as China’s economic growth slows and consumers spend less and save more, women with rising incomes are fueling the entertainment segment of the $1.5 trillion “sheconomy,” a phrase used by the Chinese government to describe women’s spending power.

尽管中国经济增长放缓、消费者减少开支并增加储蓄，但收入不断上升的女性正在推动规模达10万亿人民币的“她经济”中的娱乐消费增长。中国政府用“她经济”一词来描述女性的消费能力。

Women flush with disposable income are pursuing virtual romances with A.I. companions, playing video games that appeal to female romantic fantasies and devouring television dramas and novels featuring women as business tycoons, military commanders and political leaders — characters not traditionally portrayed by women.

拥有充裕可支配收入的女性正在与人工智能伴侣展开虚拟恋爱、玩迎合女性浪漫幻想的电子游戏，津津有味地观看大女主电视剧和小说——她们是商业大亨、军事统帅和政治领袖，而传统上这些角色并不由女性来呈现。

Among the fastest-growing offerings are sometimes risqué entertainment services that put men on display. The trend reverses the “male gaze,” in which women are objects of male desire, said Minglu Chen, an associate professor at the University of Sydney who studies gender and politics in China. Now women are paying to admire men.

增长最快的娱乐项目中，有一些以展示男性魅力为卖点，有时甚至带有几分情色意味。悉尼大学研究中国性别与政治问题的副教授陈明璐说，这一趋势颠覆了传统的“男性凝视”，在这种凝视下，女性是男性欲望的对象。如今，女性正在花钱欣赏男性。

The spending spree poses a dilemma for Beijing. For years, the government has tried to spur consumer spending to offset a prolonged property crisis. Yet its censors go into overdrive whenever feminism, gender and power become topics of national conversation. The state-owned People’s Daily recently warned businesses against “suggestive flirtation and indecent physical contact” and called for “strict regulation” after a video showing a male actor feeding a lollipop to a woman at a theme park went viral online.

这种消费热潮让北京陷入两难。多年来，政府一直试图刺激消费支出，以抵消旷日持久的房地产危机带来的影响。然而，每当女权主义、性别和权力成为全国性话题时，审查机构就会进入高度戒备状态。最近，一段主题乐园里男演员给一名女游客喂棒棒糖的视频在网上疯传，官媒《人民日报》随后警告商家不得进行“暧昧挑逗和不雅的肢体接触”，并呼吁“严格监管”。

For many women, the attention is long overdue.

对许多女性来说，这种对她们需求的关注早就该有了。

“It’s finally our turn,” said Linda Xiong, 32, an office worker who paid $90 to see a performance by the Gonggou Theater, a troupe of toned men in their 20s billed as China’s answer to the Chippendales.

32岁的办公室职员琳达·熊（音）花600块观看了公狗剧场的演出。这个剧团由20多岁、身材健硕的男性组成，被誉为美国猛男舞团奇彭代尔斯(Chippendales)的中国版。

公狗剧场在新疆的巡演，男舞者赤裸上身，身穿传统刺绣百褶裙进行表演。

在中国各地，商家正在一个利润丰厚的新兴市场掘金：女性的享乐。

Onstage, bare-chested men in traditional Chinese embroidered skirts writhe to pounding drums as women scream from the audience.

舞台上，赤裸上身的男子穿着中国传统刺绣裙装，随着震耳的鼓点扭动身体，台下的女观众发出阵阵尖叫。

“I found it incredibly joyful,” said Ms. Xiong, who is single. She noted that the show’s tickets had sold out in seven seconds. (She counted.)

“我觉得特别快乐，”单身的熊女士说。她指出，演出票七秒就售罄了。（她特意数过。）

“Whether in the past or modern times in China, wasn’t it always a group of beautiful women dancing for men?”

“中国无论是古代还是现代，不一直都是一群美女跳舞给男人看吗？”

The show is so popular that, according to its founder Junyi Ge, most of its performances in the past 15 months have sold out. A discussion forum about the show on Douyin, TikTok’s Chinese sister app, has racked up more than 2.1 billion views.

剧团创始人葛俊逸说，演出太受欢迎了，过去15个月里大多数场次的门票都是销售一空。抖音上关于该演出的话题累计浏览量已超过21亿次。

“It has to be sexy, powerful, dripping with testosterone,” Mr. Ge said in a video interview with an online influencer. “That is our secret weapon.”

“完全不回避，”葛俊逸在接受一名网络博主的视频采访时说。“就是要性感，就是要很有力量，感觉是荷尔蒙的。”

中国的主题乐园招募年轻帅气的男性，通过合影和互动游戏取悦女性游客。这些岗位没有学历要求，月薪最高可达3万元人民币。

英国伯明翰大学研究性别问题的谢凯玲说，在经济独立的中国女性中，有些人比起传统的恋爱关系更看重情感上的满足，商家正从她们的这种需求中发掘商机。

Theme parks are also realizing the power of the female gaze. Online job advertisements seek “sunny, handsome and outgoing” young men to pose for photographs and play interactive games with visitors. Some positions pay as much as $4,500 a month, more than six times the average monthly income of the country’s urban residents, with no degree required.

主题公园也意识到了“女凝”的力量。网上有招聘广告寻找“阳光、帅气、开朗”的年轻男子，与游客合影并开展互动游戏。一些岗位月薪高达3万人民币，是中国城镇居民月平均收入的六倍多，而且不要求学历。

Tour operators at some of China’s most famous mountains are hiring tall, muscular young men to wear matching uniforms, promoting them as “security guard boy groups” to draw tourists. Other young men work as freelance hiking companions, providing fresh fruit, cheering women along and sometimes carrying exhausted clients uphill in their arms.

在中国一些名山景区，旅游经营者雇用身材高大健壮的年轻男子，让他们身穿统一制服，以“保安男团”为卖点吸引游客。还有一些年轻男子以自由职业者的身份提供陪爬服务，为女性游客提供新鲜水果，一路加油打气，有时甚至把精疲力竭的客户抱上山。

Driving the boom is a generation of increasingly affluent, educated urban women shaped by three decades of China’s one-child policy.

推动这一热潮的是一代日益富裕、受过良好教育的城市女性，中国长达30年的独生子女政策塑造了这一群体。

Official statistics show that the proportion of women among first-year undergraduates has risen about 20 percentage points over the past two decades. The gender wage gap has also narrowed to 13 percent from 23 percent over the past seven years, according to reports by Zhaopin, China’s biggest job recruitment platform.

官方统计数据显示，过去20年间，本科新生中女生的占比提高了约20个百分点。中国最大的招聘平台智联招聘发布的报告还显示，过去七年间，男女薪酬差距已从23%缩小至13%。

Businesses are selling what is called “emotional value” services — or feel-good experiences — to women who are more financially independent than their mothers and grandmothers.

商家正在向经济上比母辈和祖母辈更独立的女性销售所谓的“情绪价值”服务，也就是让人获得愉悦感的体验。

这种转变并不局限于现场娱乐活动。在广受欢迎的大女主电视剧中，女性经营企业、统帅军队、掌握政治权力。

清明上河园的一名演员正在拆粉丝送的礼物，这名女粉丝则在一旁拍摄视频。

The success of these services “reflects dissatisfaction and also maybe disenchantment with romantic relationships in real life,” said Kailing Xie, an associate professor at the University of Birmingham who studies gender and society in China.

伯明翰大学研究中国性别与社会问题的副教授谢凯玲说，这些服务的成功“反映了对现实恋爱关系的不满，或许还有幻灭”。

It exposes a mismatch, she said, between women’s growing economic power and men’s slower acceptance of female expectations for intimacy in relationships.

她说，这暴露出女性的经济实力不断增强与男性未能以同样速度接受女性对亲密关系期待之间的错配。

Chenglin Liu, 21, discovered an opportunity while struggling to make ends meet as a waiter. He started charging female hikers $100 to $150 to accompany them on six-hour treks up Mount Tai in eastern China. His social media account was widely followed after he and three other guides carried a woman who had lost a leg to bone cancer all the way to the summit.

21岁的刘成林以前做服务生，收入入不敷出时发现了一个机会。他开始向女性爬山者收取600到1000元的费用，陪她们花六小时攀登中国东部的泰山。在他和另外三名导游把一名因骨癌失去一条腿的女子一路抬到山顶后，他的社交媒体账号获得了广泛关注。

但悉尼大学的陈明璐说，消费有关女性掌权的幻想并不等于真正拥有权力。凝视对象的转变“并不会改变女性在家庭、职场和政治领域的地位”。
刘成林与另一名演员参加清明上河园的巡游表演。他每天最多与200名游客合影，其中大部分是女性。
今年4月，梅丽莎·袁在安徽天柱山与一名年轻保安合影。她说，看到这些帅气的保安，她不禁露出笑容，忘记了登山的疲惫。
Melissa Yuan, 32, sees that distinction clearly.
32岁的梅丽莎·袁（音）清楚地看到了这种区别。

On a recent visit to Mount Tianzhu, near her home city of Wuhan, she reached the summit and found a line of handsome young men in sunglasses and blue-and-black uniforms. They had been hired to pose for photos with tourists.
最近，她前往距离家乡武汉不远的天柱山游玩。登顶后，她发现一排戴着墨镜、身穿蓝黑色制服的帅气年轻男子。他们受雇与游客拍照合影。
The sight made her smile. Ms. Yuan has paid good-looking men to accompany her while shopping or eating, but she does not think such transactions change the balance of power between men and women.
眼前的这一幕让她露出笑容。她曾花钱请帅哥陪自己逛街或吃饭，不过，她并不认为这类交易能够改变男女之间的权力关系。
Even when she is paying men to entertain her, she still “habitually and subconsciously” worries about their feelings.
即使是她花钱让男性取悦自己，她仍然会“习惯性地、下意识地”顾及他们的感受。
“In my experience, consumption doesn’t directly translate into power,” Ms. Yuan said.
“以我的经验，消费并不直接转化为权力，”她说。

艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)是《纽约时报》记者，主要报道中国经济及其在全球的影响。

items.body:
KEITH BRADSHER, ADAM SATARIANO2026年11月27日

2015年，中国最高领导人习近平与华为创始人任正非在伦敦。 Matthew Lloyd/PA Wire, via Associated Press

At Huawei Technologies’ headquarters in Shenzhen, China, a palatial corridor gleams with gold ceilings and elaborate frescoes of Russian aristocrats on galloping horses. It bears the name of the American president who tried to bring the Chinese technology giant to its knees.

在中国深圳的华为公司总部，一条宫殿般的走廊在金色天花板和描绘俄罗斯贵族策马奔腾的精美壁画映衬下熠熠生辉。这条走廊以那位曾试图将这家中国科技巨头逼入绝境的美国总统的名字命名。

Huawei executives call it the “Trump Corridor,” a pointed reference to President Trump’s campaign during his first term to drive the company out of global wireless networks and cut off its access to advanced chips.

华为高管称之为“特朗普走廊”，直指特朗普总统在其第一任期内发起的行动，即将华为逐出全球无线网络并切断其获取先进芯片的渠道。

The name is a gesture of defiance. Having survived punishing American sanctions, Huawei is determined to prove that Washington cannot dictate its future. That resolve faces a new test after the company was convicted this week in an American court of stealing trade secrets.

这个命名表达了拒不屈服的态度。在挺过严厉的美国制裁后，华为决心证明华盛顿无法主宰其未来。本周，该公司在美国一家法院被裁定窃取商业机密罪名成立，这一决心正面临新的考验。

In 2019, Mr. Trump’s crackdown threatened Huawei’s survival, just as it had become a world leader in telecommunications and consumer devices. Seven years later, Huawei is central to Beijing’s ambitions to challenge the United States in artificial intelligence. Its chips are the closest thing China has to an answer to Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.

2019年，正当华为成为电信和消费设备领域的全球领导者之际，特朗普的打压威胁到了该公司的生存。七年后，华为已成为北京在人工智能领域挑战美国这一抱负的核心。其芯片是中国目前最接近英伟达先进半导体的替代品。

Last month, in a vaulted conference room beyond the corridor, Ren Zhengfei, Huawei’s 82-year-old founder and chief executive, credited the American president with forcing Huawei and China into a new era of self-reliance.

上个月，在走廊尽头的一间拱顶会议室里，82岁的华为创始人兼首席执行官任正非将迫使华为和中国步入自力更生新时代归功于这位美国总统。

“Pass on our thanks to him, and also share the story of the Trump Corridor as well,” Mr. Ren said in an interview.

“请转达我们对他的感谢，也请把‘特朗普走廊’的故事分享出去，”任正非在一次采访中说。

After the U.S. crackdown, he said, Huawei cemented its identity as “a company of our own country.”

他表示，在美国打压之后，华为巩固了自己作为“我们自己国家的公司”的身份。

中国深圳华为总部的“特朗普走廊”之所以得此昵称，是为了向叫停美国对华为出口的特朗普总统表达拒不屈服的姿态。 Keith Bradsher/The New York Times

位于中国东莞的华为培训中心图书馆，其设计仿照了法国国家图书馆和国民议会图书馆。 Keith Bradsher/The New York Times

位于东莞的华为图书馆有11万册藏书。

Huawei’s resurgence illustrates a paradox in Washington’s efforts to contain China’s technological rise. The company was among the first targets of export restrictions that became a policy blueprint. American restrictions have slowed China’s advances, but they have also galvanized a national effort to dismantle the technological dependencies that gave Washington leverage.

华为的复苏凸显了华盛顿遏制中国技术崛起举措中的一个悖论。该公司是出口限制措施的首批目标之一，这些措施后来成为了一项政策蓝图。美国的限制减缓了中国的进步，但也激发了一场举国行动，以消除让华盛顿握有筹码的技术依赖。

On Tuesday, after an 11-week trial, a federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets from American companies and evading sanctions against Iran. Huawei said the verdicts were “without legal or factual merit.”

周二，经过11周的审理，一个联邦陪审团裁定华为窃取美国公司商业机密和逃避对伊朗制裁的罪名成立。华为表示，这些裁决“缺乏法律和事实依据”。

As its American ties unravel, Huawei is becoming more indispensable to China. This month, the Trump administration announced plans to block Chinese companies from accessing advanced A.I. chips through overseas data centers, closing one of the last routes to Nvidia’s most powerful semiconductors.

随着与美国的联系逐渐瓦解，华为对中国变得越来越不可或缺。本月，特朗普政府宣布计划阻止中国企业通过海外数据中心获取先进人工智能芯片，堵住了获取英伟达最强大半导体的最后途径之一。

The move comes amid turmoil at Nvidia. Jensen Huang, its chief executive, resigned two weeks ago following allegations of an affair with an executive at the Singaporean data center company Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence officials believe the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with a Chinese Ministry of State Security officer during their relationship. Beijing has denied spying.

这一举措出台之际，英伟达正陷入动荡。公司首席执行官黄仁勋两周前因被指与新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed的一名高管有染而辞职。美国情报官员认为，这位名为黄乐(Alice Huang)的女性在两人婚外情期间曾与中国国家安全部的一名官员有联系。北京方面否认从事间谍活动。

This week, Mr. Huang returned as chief executive after a pressure campaign by President Trump, who said the reversal was necessary to ensure the “success and prosperity” of Nvidia and the American economy.

本周，在特朗普总统的施压下，黄仁勋重返首席执行官岗位。特朗普表示，这一逆转对于确保英伟达和美国经济的“成功与繁荣”十分必要。

Before the upheaval at Nvidia, Mr. Ren acknowledged the challenge of building an advanced semiconductor supply chain but predicted that China would eventually surpass the United States.

在英伟达发生动荡之前，任正非承认建立先进半导体供应链面临挑战，但预测中国最终将超越美国。

“It’s just a matter of time,” he said.

“只是时间问题，”他说。

今年，英伟达芯片预计提供的人工智能算力将是华为的25倍以上。

本月早些时候，顾客在位于深圳万象城的华为旗舰店内。

Huawei’s annual spending on research and development now exceeds $27 billion. Its Ascend processors have become China’s leading alternative to Nvidia’s A.I. chips. Beyond designing chips, it is assembling the infrastructure to become one of the world’s biggest chip makers.

华为目前的年研发支出超过270亿美元。其昇腾处理器已成为中国替代英伟达人工智能芯片的首要选择。除了设计芯片，华为还在整合基础设施，以成为全球最大的芯片制造商之一。

It has brought together suppliers, government-backed factories and equipment makers, built data centers and worked with Chinese A.I. companies, including DeepSeek, to adapt their models to its chips.

该公司联合了供应商、政府支持的工厂和设备制造商，建设了数据中心，并与包括DeepSeek在内的中国人工智能公司合作，使其模型适配华为芯片。

The technological gulf remains enormous. Huawei’s chips are expected to deliver less than 4 percent of Nvidia’s A.I. computing power this year, and Huawei is unlikely to match Nvidia’s current output until around 2030, according to the research firm Epoch AI.

技术鸿沟依然巨大。根据研究机构Epoch AI的数据，华为芯片今年预计提供的人工智能算力不到英伟达的4%，而且不太可能在2030年左右之前追上英伟达目前的产出水平。

“Huawei is pulling on every single lever available to them and they are pulling hard,” said Venkat Somala, an analyst with Epoch AI, who recently published a report on the company. “The question is, will it be enough?”

“华为正在动用所有可用的手段，非常努力，”最近就华为写了一份报告的Epoch AI分析师文卡特·索马拉表示，“问题是，这够吗？”

‘Survival First’

“生存第一”

When Mr. Trump approved sweeping restrictions on Huawei in his first term, many in his administration believed they could destroy the company, which officials feared was aiding China’s military.

当特朗普在第一任期内批准对华为实施全面限制时，其政府中的许多人认为这可能会摧毁这家公司，官员们担心该公司正在协助中国军方。

“We thought this could be a death blow,” said Liza Tobin, who worked on China policy on the National Security Council at the time. “It hobbled them and broke their leg and slowed them down. But now they have regrouped.”

“我们曾以为这可能是致命一击，”当时在国家安全委员会负责对华政策的丽莎·托宾说，“事实上确实束缚了他们，打断了他们的腿，减缓了他们的速度。但现在他们已经重整旗鼓。”

Xi Jinping, China’s leader, responded by vowing to build a domestic technology supply chain.

中国领导人习近平对此作出回应，誓言建立本土技术供应链。

“It’s a new Long March now, and we must start all over again,” he said, invoking the Communist Party’s arduous retreat in the 1930s before its rise to power.

“现在是新的长征，我们要重新再出发，”他说，其中的“长征”指的是中国共产党在20世纪30年代获得政权前那场艰苦的战略转移。

Before the crackdown, Huawei was deeply embedded in the global technology supply chain. It bought $2.5 billion worth of chips annually from Intel and was one of the largest customers of Oracle and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading chip maker, according to Huawei.

在遭到打压之前，华为深度融入全球技术供应链。据华为称，该公司每年从英特尔购买价值25亿美元的芯片，并且是甲骨文和全球领先芯片制造商台积电的最大客户之一。

“After the U.S. sanctions, our pursuits have been survival first,” Mr. Ren said.

“美国制裁后，我们的追求一直是生存第一，”任正非说。

Mr. Ren knows something about survival. Growing up in one of China’s poorest provinces, he endured the great famine of the early 1960s. During the Cultural Revolution, his father, a schoolteacher, was denounced as a “capitalist roadster” and confined in a cow barn.

任正非深谙生存之道。他成长于中国最贫困的省份之一，经历了20世纪60年代初的大饥荒。“文化大革命”期间，他担任学校教师的父亲被打成“走资派”，关进牛棚。

Mr. Ren joined the army, rose to become deputy director of a military-run research institute and founded Huawei after China disbanded the military’s construction corps in 1983.

任正非参过军，曾升任一家军办研究所的副所长，并在1983年中国解散基建工程兵后创立了华为。

The showdown with Washington has also been personal. In December 2018, Mr. Ren’s daughter, Meng Wanzhou, then Huawei’s chief financial officer, was arrested in Vancouver at the request of U.S. law enforcement. It was part of a case that culminated in this week’s guilty verdict against the company. She spent nearly three years under house arrest before a deal allowed her to return to China.

与华盛顿的对决也波及了他的个人生活。2018年12月，任正非的女儿、时任华为首席财务官的孟晚舟应美国执法部门的要求在温哥华被捕。这是导致本周该公司被判有罪的案件的一部分。她被软禁了近三年，直到一项协议允许她返回中国。

2023年，华为首席财务官兼副董事长孟晚舟在上海。

位于比利时鲁汶的研究机构微电子研究中心内的阿斯麦芯片制造设备，这种设备将助力未来几代计算机芯片的开发和商业化。

Huawei executives have seen a shift in Mr. Ren as a result of the U.S. campaign. “The U.S. government hasn’t yet realized that this move is turning someone who was most pro-American into someone who is anti-American,” said Gavin Gai, Huawei’s corporate strategy director, before clarifying that Mr. Ren is not anti-American.

华为高管们看到了任正非在美国打压行动下发生的转变。“美国政府还没有意识到，此举正在把一个最亲美的人变成一个反美的人，”在华为负责企业战略的盖刚说，随后他又澄清任正非并不反美。

Around 2021, Mr. Ren accelerated efforts to build a domestic semiconductor supply chain, working with China’s Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, known as SMIC, as well as research institutes and other domestic firms.

2021年前后，任正非加快了建立本土半导体供应链的步伐，与中国的中芯国际以及研究机构和其他本土企业展开合作。

The biggest obstacle is manufacturing, not design. China still lacks the most sophisticated chip-making equipment, including lithography machines made by the Dutch company ASML that print microscopic circuit patterns onto silicon wafers.

最大的障碍在于制造，而非设计。中国仍然缺乏最精密的芯片制造设备，包括荷兰公司阿斯麦生产的光刻机，这种设备能将微小的电路图案印刻在硅晶圆上。

Huawei says it can eventually rival Nvidia’s systems by linking many less powerful processors.

华为表示，通过连接大量性能相对弱的处理器，最终可以与英伟达的系统相抗衡。

Liang Wenfeng, chief executive of DeepSeek, the Chinese start-up that stunned Silicon Valley with its inexpensive, powerful A.I. model, estimated Huawei’s technology was about two years behind Nvidia’s, according to excerpts from a leaked investor call published by Chinese media outlets.

据中国媒体公布的一份泄露的投资者电话会议纪要摘录，以低成本、高性能人工智能模型震惊硅谷的中国初创公司DeepSeek的首席执行官梁文锋估计，华为的技术大约落后英伟达两年。

Huawei may not need to match Nvidia’s technology to dominate the Chinese market. American restrictions and Beijing’s push for self-reliance are steering Chinese companies toward domestic suppliers.

华为或许不需要在技术上匹敌英伟达就能主导中国市场。美国的限制和北京对自力更生的推动正引导中国企业转向本土供应商。

Martin Lau, the president of Tencent, the Chinese internet giant, said losing access to advanced Nvidia chips “sets everyone back in China” in A.I. development. The priority now, he told investors, must be “speeding up the domestic supply chain.”

中国互联网巨头腾讯的总裁刘炽平表示，无法获取先进的英伟达芯片“让中国的所有人都倒退了”。他告诉投资者，现在的当务之急必须是“加速国内半导体供应链的发展”。

Beijing has reinforced that imperative by blocking imports of Nvidia chips and pressing Chinese companies to buy domestic alternatives. On Nov. 17, Nvidia announced that it was halting sales to China altogether.

北京通过阻止英伟达芯片进口并敦促中国企业购买本土替代品，强化了这一紧迫任务。11月17日，英伟达宣布全面暂停对华销售。

华为东莞培训中心仿照欧洲村镇建造，为公司员工提供了一个国际化的环境。

东莞华为智能手机工厂的工人在午休时间离开工厂。

On The Factory Floor

工厂车间里

Inside a Huawei factory in southern China, a hall stretching the length of one and a half football fields hums with a dozen smartphone assembly lines.

在中国南方的一家华为工厂，一个长达一个半足球场的车间里，十几条智能手机组装线正嗡嗡作响。

What is striking is how few people are there.

引人注目的是，这里的人少之又少。

Each line employs nine workers in white lab coats and baseball caps, down from nearly 90 a dozen years ago. Robots occupy the workstations, while A.I.-powered cameras inspect production of each Mate 90 Pro smartphone, from soldering circuit boards to final assembly.

每条生产线配备九名身穿白色实验服、头戴棒球帽的工人，而十几年前这一数字接近90人。机器人占据了工位，由人工智能驱动的摄像头检查着每部Mate 90 Pro智能手机从电路板焊接到最终组装的生产过程。

If a worker’s hands make the wrong movement, a computer sounds an alarm and prevents the phone from advancing.

如果工人的手部有错误动作，计算机就会发出警报，并阻止手机进入下一道工序。

China’s success in A.I. may depend less on building the most powerful models than on deploying the technology across its vast industrial economy.

或许，中国在人工智能领域的成功与其说取决于打造最强大的模型，不如说取决于将该技术部署到其庞大的工业经济中。

While Silicon Valley races to develop systems capable of surpassing human intelligence, Huawei is championing Beijing’s “A.I. Plus” strategy, using the technology to improve productivity across industries. China already manufactures more goods than the United States, Germany, Japan, South Korea and Britain combined.

当硅谷竞相开发能够超越人类智能的系统时，华为正在大力推动北京的“人工智能+”战略，利用该技术提高各行各业的生产力。中国目前制造的商品已超过美国、德国、日本、韩国和英国的总和。

Across China, Huawei’s survival has become a lesson in withstanding American pressure. Mr. Ren said he still hoped the United States and China could repair their relationship.

在中国，华为的生存已成为抵御美国压力的一堂课。任正非表示，他仍然希望美中两国能够修复关系。

However, “we have now established a complete chain that allows us to survive.”

不过，“我们现在已经建立起了一条能让我们活下去的完整链条。”

Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。

Adam Satariano是时报科技记者，常驻伦敦。

这个命名表达了拒不屈服的态度。在挺过严厉的美国制裁后，华为决心证明华盛顿无法主宰其未来。本周，该公司在美国一家法院被裁定窃取商业机密罪名成立，这一决心正面临新的考验。

In 2019, Mr. Trump’s crackdown threatened Huawei’s survival, just as it had become a world leader in telecommunications and consumer devices. Seven years later, Huawei is central to Beijing’s ambitions to challenge the United States in artificial intelligence. Its chips are the closest thing China has to an answer to Nvidia's advanced semiconductors.
2019年，正当华为成为电信和消费设备领域的全球领导者之际，特朗普的打压威胁到了该公司的生存。七年后，华为已成为北京在人工智能领域挑战美国这一抱负的核心。其芯片是中国目前最接近英伟达先进半导体的替代品。

Last month, in a vaulted conference room beyond the corridor, Ren Zhengfei, Huawei’s 82-year-old founder and chief executive, credited the American president with forcing Huawei and China into a new era of self-reliance.
上个月，在走廊尽头的一间拱顶会议室里，82岁的华为创始人兼首席执行官任正非将迫使华为和中国步入自力更生新时代归功于这位美国总统。
“Pass on our thanks to him, and also share the story of the Trump Corridor as well,” Mr. Ren said in an interview.
“请转达我们对他的感谢，也请把‘特朗普走廊’的故事分享出去，”任正非在一次采访中说。
After the U.S. crackdown, he said, Huawei cemented its identity as “a company of our own country.”
他表示，在美国打压之后，华为巩固了自己作为“我们自己国家的公司”的身份。
中国深圳华为总部的“特朗普走廊”之所以得此昵称，是为了向叫停美国对华为出口的特朗普总统表达拒不屈服的姿态。 Keith Bradsher/The New York Times
位于中国东莞的华为培训中心图书馆，其设计仿照了法国国家图书馆和国民议会图书馆。 Keith Bradsher/The New York Times
位于东莞的华为图书馆有11万册藏书。

Huawei’s resurgence illustrates a paradox in Washington’s efforts to contain China’s technological rise. The company was among the first targets of export restrictions that became a policy blueprint. American restrictions have slowed China’s advances, but they have also galvanized a national effort to dismantle the technological dependencies that gave Washington leverage.
华为的复苏凸显了华盛顿遏制中国技术崛起举措中的一个悖论。该公司是出口限制措施的首批目标之一，这些措施后来成为了一项政策蓝图。美国的限制减缓了中国的进步，但也激发了一场举国行动，以消除让华盛顿握有筹码的技术依赖。

On Tuesday, after an 11-week trial, a federal jury found Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets from American companies and evading sanctions against Iran. Huawei said the verdicts were “without legal or factual merit.”
周二，经过11周的审理，一个联邦陪审团裁定华为窃取美国公司商业机密和逃避对伊朗制裁的罪名成立。华为表示，这些裁决“缺乏法律和事实依据”。

As its American ties unravel, Huawei is becoming more indispensable to China. This month, the Trump administration announced plans to block Chinese companies from accessing advanced A.I. chips through overseas data centers, closing one of the last routes to Nvidia’s most powerful semiconductors.
随着与美国的联系逐渐瓦解，华为对中国变得越来越不可或缺。本月，特朗普政府宣布计划阻止中国企业通过海外数据中心获取先进人工智能芯片，堵住了获取英伟达最强大半导体的最后途径之一。

The move comes amid turmoil at Nvidia. Jensen Huang, its chief executive, resigned two weeks ago following allegations of an affair with an executive at the Singaporean data center company Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence officials believe the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with a Chinese Ministry of State Security officer during their relationship. Beijing has denied spying.
这一举措出台之际，英伟达正陷入动荡。公司首席执行官黄仁勋两周前因被指与新加坡数据中心公司Megaspeed的一名高管有染而辞职。美国情报官员认为，这位名为黄乐(Alice Huang)的女性在两人婚外情期间曾与中国国家安全部的一名官员有联系。北京方面否认从事间谍活动。

This week, Mr. Huang returned as chief executive after a pressure campaign by President Trump, who said the reversal was necessary to ensure the “success and prosperity” of Nvidia and the American economy.
本周，在特朗普总统的施压下，黄仁勋重返首席执行官岗位。特朗普表示，这一逆转对于确保英伟达和美国经济的“成功与繁荣”十分必要。
Before the upheaval at Nvidia, Mr. Ren acknowledged the challenge of building an advanced semiconductor supply chain but predicted that China would eventually surpass the United States.
在英伟达发生动荡之前，任正非承认建立先进半导体供应链面临挑战，但预测中国最终将超越美国。
“It’s just a matter of time,” he said.
“只是时间问题，”他说。
今年，英伟达芯片预计提供的人工智能算力将是华为的25倍以上。
本月早些时候，顾客在位于深圳万象城的华为旗舰店内。

Huawei’s annual spending on research and development now exceeds $27 billion. Its Ascend processors have become China’s leading alternative to Nvidia’s A.I. chips. Beyond designing chips, it is assembling the infrastructure to become one of the world’s biggest chip makers.
华为目前的年研发支出超过270亿美元。其昇腾处理器已成为中国替代英伟达人工智能芯片的首要选择。除了设计芯片，华为还在整合基础设施，以成为全球最大的芯片制造商之一。
It has brought together suppliers, government-backed factories and equipment makers, built data centers and worked with Chinese A.I. companies, including DeepSeek, to adapt their models to its chips.
该公司联合了供应商、政府支持的工厂和设备制造商，建设了数据中心，并与包括DeepSeek在内的中国人工智能公司合作，使其模型适配华为芯片。

The technological gulf remains enormous. Huawei’s chips are expected to deliver less than 4 percent of Nvidia’s A.I. computing power this year, and Huawei is unlikely to match Nvidia’s current output until around 2030, according to the research firm Epoch AI.
技术鸿沟依然巨大。根据研究机构Epoch AI的数据，华为芯片今年预计提供的人工智能算力不到英伟达的4%，而且不太可能在2030年左右之前追上英伟达目前的产出水平。

“Huawei is pulling on every single lever available to them and they are pulling hard,” said Venkat Somala, an analyst with Epoch AI, who recently published a report on the company. “The question is, will it be enough?”
“华为正在动用所有可用的手段，非常努力，”最近就华为写了一份报告的Epoch AI分析师文卡特·索马拉表示，“问题是，这够吗？”
‘Survival First’
“生存第一”
When Mr. Trump approved sweeping restrictions on Huawei in his first term, many in his administration believed they could destroy the company, which officials feared was aiding China’s military.
当特朗普在第一任期内批准对华为实施全面限制时，其政府中的许多人认为这可能会摧毁这家公司，官员们担心该公司正在协助中国军方。

“We thought this could be a death blow,” said Liza Tobin, who worked on China policy on the National Security Council at the time. “It hobbled them and broke their leg and slowed them down. But now they have regrouped.”
“我们曾以为这可能是致命一击，”当时在国家安全委员会负责对华政策的丽莎·托宾说，“事实上确实束缚了他们，打断了他们的腿，减缓了他们的速度。但现在他们已经重整旗鼓。”
Xi Jinping, China’s leader, responded by vowing to build a domestic technology supply chain.
中国领导人习近平对此作出回应，誓言建立本土技术供应链。
“It’s a new Long March now, and we must start all over again,” he said, invoking the Communist Party’s arduous retreat in the 1930s before its rise to power.
“现在是新的长征，我们要重新再出发，”他说，其中的“长征”指的是中国共产党在20世纪30年代获得政权前那场艰苦的战略转移。

Before the crackdown, Huawei was deeply embedded in the global technology supply chain. It bought $2.5 billion worth of chips annually from Intel and was one of the largest customers of Oracle and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading chip maker, according to Huawei.
在遭到打压之前，华为深度融入全球技术供应链。据华为称，该公司每年从英特尔购买价值25亿美元的芯片，并且是甲骨文和全球领先芯片制造商台积电的最大客户之一。
“After the U.S. sanctions, our pursuits have been survival first,” Mr. Ren said.
“美国制裁后，我们的追求一直是生存第一，”任正非说。

Mr. Ren knows something about survival. Growing up in one of China’s poorest provinces, he endured the great famine of the early 1960s. During the Cultural Revolution, his father, a schoolteacher, was denounced as a “capitalist roadster” and confined in a cow barn.
任正非深谙生存之道。他成长于中国最贫困的省份之一，经历了20世纪60年代初的大饥荒。“文化大革命”期间，他担任学校教师的父亲被打成“走资派”，关进牛棚。
Mr. Ren joined the army, rose to become deputy director of a military-run research institute and founded Huawei after China disbanded the military’s construction corps in 1983.
任正非参过军，曾升任一家军办研究所的副所长，并在1983年中国解散基建工程兵后创立了华为。

The showdown with Washington has also been personal. In December 2018, Mr. Ren’s daughter, Meng Wanzhou, then Huawei’s chief financial officer, was arrested in Vancouver at the request of U.S. law enforcement. It was part of a case that culminated in this week’s guilty verdict against the company. She spent nearly three years under house arrest before a deal allowed her to return to China.
与华盛顿的对决也波及了他的个人生活。2018年12月，任正非的女儿、时任华为首席财务官的孟晚舟应美国执法部门的要求在温哥华被捕。这是导致本周该公司被判有罪的案件的一部分。她被软禁了近三年，直到一项协议允许她返回中国。
2023年，华为首席财务官兼副董事长孟晚舟在上海。
位于比利时鲁汶的研究机构微电子研究中心内的阿斯麦芯片制造设备，这种设备将助力未来几代计算机芯片的开发和商业化。

Huawei executives have seen a shift in Mr. Ren as a result of the U.S. campaign. “The U.S. government hasn’t yet realized that this move is turning someone who was most pro-American into someone who is anti-American,” said Gavin Gai, Huawei’s corporate strategy director, before clarifying that Mr. Ren is not anti-American.
华为高管们看到了任正非在美国打压行动下发生的转变。“美国政府还没有意识到，此举正在把一个最亲美的人变成一个反美的人，”在华为负责企业战略的盖刚说，随后他又澄清任正非并不反美。

Around 2021, Mr. Ren accelerated efforts to build a domestic semiconductor supply chain, working with China’s Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, known as SMIC, as well as research institutes and other domestic firms.
2021年前后，任正非加快了建立本土半导体供应链的步伐，与中国的中芯国际以及研究机构和其他本土企业展开合作。

The biggest obstacle is manufacturing, not design. China still lacks the most sophisticated chip-making equipment, including lithography machines made by the Dutch company ASML that print microscopic circuit patterns onto silicon wafers.
最大的障碍在于制造，而非设计。中国仍然缺乏最精密的芯片制造设备，包括荷兰公司阿斯麦生产的光刻机，这种设备能将微小的电路图案印刻在硅晶圆上。
Huawei says it can eventually rival Nvidia’s systems by linking many less powerful processors.
华为表示，通过连接大量性能相对弱的处理器，最终可以与英伟达的系统相抗衡。

Liang Wenfeng, chief executive of DeepSeek, the Chinese start-up that stunned Silicon Valley with its inexpensive, powerful A.I. model, estimated Huawei’s technology was about two years behind Nvidia’s, according to excerpts from a leaked investor call published by Chinese media outlets.
据中国媒体公布的一份泄露的投资者电话会议纪要摘录，以低成本、高性能人工智能模型震惊硅谷的中国初创公司DeepSeek的首席执行官梁文锋估计，华为的技术大约落后英伟达两年。
Huawei may not need to match Nvidia’s technology to dominate the Chinese market. American restrictions and Beijing’s push for self-reliance are steering Chinese companies toward domestic suppliers.
华为或许不需要在技术上匹敌英伟达就能主导中国市场。美国的限制和北京对自力更生的推动正引导中国企业转向本土供应商。

Martin Lau, the president of Tencent, the Chinese internet giant, said losing access to advanced Nvidia chips “sets everyone back in China” in A.I. development. The priority now, he told investors, must be “speeding up the domestic supply chain.”
中国互联网巨头腾讯的总裁刘炽平表示，无法获取先进的英伟达芯片“让中国的所有人都倒退了”。他告诉投资者，现在的当务之急必须是“加速国内半导体供应链的发展”。

Beijing has reinforced that imperative by blocking imports of Nvidia chips and pressing Chinese companies to buy domestic alternatives. On Nov. 17, Nvidia announced that it was halting sales to China altogether.
北京通过阻止英伟达芯片进口并敦促中国企业购买本土替代品，强化了这一紧迫任务。11月17日，英伟达宣布全面暂停对华销售。
华为东莞培训中心仿照欧洲村镇建造，为公司员工提供了一个国际化的环境。
东莞华为智能手机工厂的工人在午休时间离开工厂。
On The Factory Floor
工厂车间里
Inside a Huawei factory in southern China, a hall stretching the length of one and a half football fields hums with a dozen smartphone assembly lines.
在中国南方的一家华为工厂，一个长达一个半足球场的车间里，十几条智能手机组装线正嗡嗡作响。
What is striking is how few people are there.
引人注目的是，这里的人少之又少。

Each line employs nine workers in white lab coats and baseball caps, down from nearly 90 a dozen years ago. Robots occupy the workstations, while A.I.-powered cameras inspect production of each Mate 90 Pro smartphone, from soldering circuit boards to final assembly.
每条生产线配备九名身穿白色实验服、头戴棒球帽的工人，而十几年前这一数字接近90人。机器人占据了工位，由人工智能驱动的摄像头检查着每部Mate 90 Pro智能手机从电路板焊接到最终组装的生产过程。
If a worker’s hands make the wrong movement, a computer sounds an alarm and prevents the phone from advancing.
如果工人的手部有错误动作，计算机就会发出警报，并阻止手机进入下一道工序。
China’s success in A.I. may depend less on building the most powerful models than on deploying the technology across its vast industrial economy.
或许，中国在人工智能领域的成功与其说取决于打造最强大的模型，不如说取决于将该技术部署到其庞大的工业经济中。

While Silicon Valley races to develop systems capable of surpassing human intelligence, Huawei is championing Beijing’s “A.I. Plus” strategy, using the technology to improve productivity across industries. China already manufactures more goods than the United States, Germany, Japan, South Korea and Britain combined.
当硅谷竞相开发能够超越人类智能的系统时，华为正在大力推动北京的“人工智能+”战略，利用该技术提高各行各业的生产力。中国目前制造的商品已超过美国、德国、日本、韩国和英国的总和。
Across China, Huawei’s survival has become a lesson in withstanding American pressure. Mr. Ren said he still hoped the United States and China could repair their relationship.
在中国，华为的生存已成为抵御美国压力的一堂课。任正非表示，他仍然希望美中两国能够修复关系。
However, “we have now established a complete chain that allows us to survive.”
不过，“我们现在已经建立起了一条能让我们活下去的完整链条。”
Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。
Adam Satariano是时报科技记者，常驻伦敦。

items.body:
香港突发撞船事故，至少24人受伤，大批救护车在场戒备

香港警方27日向新华社记者证实，当天上午9时21分接报，青衣路对开海域发生船只意外。一艘由香港上环开往蛇口的船只撞到青衣油库附近硬物，造成至少24人受伤，其中4人伤势严重，目前全部伤者意识清醒。

救援人员已赶赴现场协助，消防处出动消防船及流动伤者治疗车，大批救护车在场戒备。事故原因正在调查中。据新华社

items.body:
酒店回应女子因超40岁被拒入住

11月26日，有网友发视频吐槽，她之前入住浙江嘉兴一家酒店时，因年龄超过40岁被拒绝办理入住，只能转去其他酒店。当事人李女士介绍，她11月19日从苏州乘高铁前往嘉兴，当晚7点左右抵达，在网上预订了勤俭路的荔枝酒店。#女子因超40岁被酒店拒办入住#

“到酒店后我拿出身份证办理入住，工作人员问我年龄，我说57岁，对方就说他们酒店床位房仅限18至40岁客人入住，还说各预订平台都标注了这条信息。但我下单的时候确实没有看到相关年龄限制。我后来找老板沟通，老板依旧拒绝我入住，最后我只能换别的酒店。”李女士说，“当时我挺生气的，酒店最后给我的解释是床铺太高，担心发生危险。”

26日下午，记者以游客身份致电荔枝酒店（嘉兴月河店），工作人员证实，酒店确实有年龄限制，40岁以上不能入住，是酒店老板规定的，但她并不清楚设立年龄限制的具体原因。记者随后又咨询嘉兴多家青旅酒店，遇见青旅（万达广场店）工作人员表示，他们门店没有年龄限制，可正常办理入住。嘉兴秀湖青年旅社工作人员称，会看客人身体状况，身体条件允许就可以入住，记者留意到，这家酒店在线上平台的售卖页面标注了“限18-55岁客人入住”。
